<description>
The Risks section of `doc/REST-interface.md` describes the wrong way for a web page to read the REST interface.

It says a page can read the node with `<script src="http://127.0.0.1:8332/rest/tx/....json">`. A JSON object is not a valid script, so that reads nothing. The server accepts any `Host` header. A page whose domain name is later made to resolve to `127.0.0.1` (DNS rebinding) can therefore read the interface with same-origin requests. I changed the text to say that. A `Host` check would also stop this, but it needs a list of allowed names, so I left it out. I checked that a REST request with `Host: evil.example` gets a 200. I did not run a rebinding page.

This is one of several PRs from a large audit of Bitcoin Core that I did with the help of LLM tools. The audit produced its evidence all at once, which is why the PRs arrive together. I understand each change fully and will answer review questions myself.
</description>

005723fc78 doc: describe REST browser risk as DNS rebinding

The Risks section of REST-interface.md says a page can read the node
with a script tag pointing at /rest/tx/....json. A JSON object is not a
valid script, so that does not work.

The risk that does exist is DNS rebinding: the server accepts any Host
header, so a page whose domain name is made to resolve to 127.0.0.1 can
read the REST interface with same-origin requests. I changed the text
to say that.
</commits>
